skills.name: Review: the simple structure of the atom

note.text:
All matter is made of tiny particles called atoms. An atom has:
• a very small, dense nucleus at the centre, containing protons (positive) and neutrons (no charge);
• electrons (negative) moving around the nucleus in shells (energy levels).
An atom is electrically neutral: number of protons = number of electrons.
The number of protons is the atomic number (Z); protons + neutrons is the mass number (A). Neutrons = A − Z.

sections.heading: Inside an atom
sections.text:
Everything around you, the air, water, the wood of your desk, is made of atoms. They are far too small to see: millions of them would fit across the full stop at the end of this sentence.
An atom has a tiny, heavy centre called the nucleus. Around it, much lighter particles called electrons move in shells (energy levels).

sections.heading: Three particles
sections.text:
• Protons: in the nucleus, positive charge.
• Neutrons: in the nucleus, no charge.
• Electrons: in the shells, negative charge, very light.
An atom has the same number of electrons as protons, so the charges cancel: the atom is neutral.
Almost all the mass of an atom is in the nucleus, but almost all its volume is the space where the electrons move.

sections.heading: Atomic number and mass number
sections.text:
The atomic number (Z) is the number of protons. It decides which element the atom is: every atom with {6} protons is carbon.
The mass number (A) is the number of protons plus neutrons.
So neutrons = A − Z. A sodium atom (Z = {11}, A = {23}) has {11} protons, {11} electrons and {12} neutrons.

key_words.meaning: the small, dense centre of an atom
negative particle moving around the nucleus

mistake.right: Electrons = protons = atomic number (in a neutral atom)
mistake.why: The mass number counts protons and neutrons together.

worked_example.problem: A sodium atom has atomic number {atomicNumber(X)} and mass number {massNumber(X)}. How many protons, electrons and neutrons does it have?
steps: The atom is neutral, so electrons = protons = {atomicNumber(X)}.

cards.idea: Protons and neutrons are in the nucleus; electrons move around it in shells.
example: Hydrogen has {1} proton and {1} electron and no neutron.

cards.idea: In a neutral atom, the number of electrons equals the number of protons.

check.prompt: An atom of {nameOf(X)} has atomic number {atomicNumber(X)} and mass number {massNumber(X)}. How many neutrons does it have?

misconceptions.explain: Subtract the atomic number from the mass number.
That is the number of protons.

pick.q: Where are the protons in an atom?
w: in the shells around the nucleus
e: The nucleus is a tiny dense centre.
All particles of an atom are inside it.
pick.y: Protons and neutrons make up the nucleus.

pick.q: Which particle moves around the nucleus?
e: The nucleus is the centre itself.
pick.y: Electrons move in shells around the nucleus.

pick.q: Why is an atom electrically neutral?
pick.r: It has equal numbers of protons and electrons
w: It has no particles with charge
It has equal numbers of protons and neutrons
e: Neutrons have no charge, so they do not balance anything.
pick.y: Each proton's + charge is balanced by an electron's − charge.

questions.prompt: An atom of {nameOf(X)} has atomic number {atomicNumber(X)}. How many electrons does it have?

misconceptions.explain: The mass number counts protons and neutrons. Electrons = atomic number.

solution: The atom is neutral: electrons = protons = atomic number.

questions.prompt: An atom of {nameOf(X)} has atomic number {atomicNumber(X)} and mass number {massNumber(X)}. How many neutrons does it have?

misconceptions.explain: Subtract the atomic number from the mass number.
That is the number of protons.

questions.prompt: An atom has {p} protons and {n} neutrons. What is its mass number?

misconceptions.explain: Add protons and neutrons: both are in the nucleus.

pick.q: Most of the mass of an atom is in…
e: Electrons are very light (about 1/1840 of a proton).
The outer shell holds only light electrons.
pick.y: Protons and neutrons are much heavier than electrons.

pick.q: Most of the volume of an atom is…
e: The nucleus is tiny compared with the atom.
Neutrons are in the tiny nucleus.
Protons are in the tiny nucleus.
pick.y: Electrons move in a large space around a tiny nucleus.

pick.q: Which statement about the nucleus is correct?
e: The protons give it a positive charge.
pick.y: Protons give the nucleus its positive charge.
